binders: An implicit real m by m matrix A indexed by Fin m.
hypotheses: A is hyperbolic in the encoded sense: there exist real eigenvalues lambda_p and a real basis (v_p) indexed by Fin m such that A v_p=lambda_p v_p for every p.
conclusions: There exist real eigenvalues lambda_p and an eigenbasis (v_p) satisfying A v_p=lambda_p v_p for every p.
For every vector q in Real^m, there exists a unique amplitude function a:Fin m->Real such that sum over all p of a_p v_p equals q.
mathematical_definitions: Vectors are functions Fin m -> Real.
The eigenbasis is a Module.Basis (Fin m) Real (Fin m -> Real), not merely an arbitrary family.
The expansion sum is over Finset.univ, hence all m basis indices.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Every real m by m matrix that possesses a complete real eigenbasis admits a choice of real eigenvalues and eigenbasis for which each vector q has one and only one coefficient function a satisfying q=sum_p a_p v_p.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The hypothesis uses a strong hyperbolicity notion: diagonalizability over the reals by a full eigenbasis.
No symmetry, distinctness or ordering of eigenvalues, normalization or orientation of eigenvectors, or uniqueness of the chosen eigenbasis and eigenvalues is asserted.
Only amplitudes relative to the selected basis are unique.
The dimension m may be zero; then the empty vector space, empty basis, and empty coefficient function make the statement meaningful and noncontradictory.
The result is an algebraic basis-expansion statement and encodes no PDE, spatial variable, regularity, or characteristic evolution.
